description: Implement the 'Why Kelza Can Win' competitive advantages section (investor question 9) as a new section after why-now-section. Create css/competitive.css, js/sections/CompetitiveSection.js, add the HTML section to index.html, wire imports in css/main.css and js/app.js.
steps: Create css/competitive.css following the exact BEM + design-token pattern from css/why-now.css. Use .competitive-section as root, .competitive--visible for show, .competitive__element--revealed for child reveals. Include styles for: container, intro heading/description, five advantage cards (community graph, trust graph, AI learning loop, creator ecosystem, platform flywheel), the flywheel SVG (visually distinct from business section flywheel - use --color-brand-secondary (#06b6d4) stroke instead of --color-brand-primary to differentiate), and the bridge/transition text. Use CSS Grid for the advantage card layout (1col mobile, 2col 768px, 3col 1024px). Include responsive breakpoints (768px, 1024px) and reduced motion media query.

Create js/sections/CompetitiveSection.js following WhyNowSection.js exactly: export class CompetitiveSection with constructor (gets #competitive-section element), _setupObserver (IntersectionObserver on [data-reveal] children, adds 'competitive__element--revealed' on 0.15 ratio), reveal() (removes aria-hidden, adds competitive--visible, calls _setupObserver), hide() (re-adds aria-hidden, removes competitive--visible, disconnects observer, removes revealed classes), isVisible(), destroy(). Keep under 400 lines and no function over 60 lines.

Add the new section HTML to index.html AFTER the closing </section> of why-now-section (id='why-now-section') and BEFORE </main>. Section id='competitive-section', class='competitive-section', aria-label='Why Kelza can win - competitive advantages', aria-hidden='true'. Structure: container div, intro div with h2 heading '[Why Kelza Can Win]' and description, then five advantage blocks each with [data-reveal], h3 heading, description paragraph, and supporting detail. The fifth advantage (Platform Flywheel) includes an inline SVG with 7 nodes in a circular layout (Better Communities -> Better Experiences -> More Engagement -> More Creators -> Better Marketplace -> More Value -> Better Communities). End with bridge div containing '[Now let us understand the size of the opportunity.]'.
Add @import './competitive.css'; to css/main.css after the existing @import './why-now.css'; line.

In js/app.js: add import { CompetitiveSection } from './sections/CompetitiveSection.js'; after the WhyNowSection import. Inside DOMContentLoaded callback, after whyNowSection.reveal(), add: const competitiveSection = new CompetitiveSection(); competitiveSection.reveal();
acceptance_criteria: css/competitive.css exists and uses only design tokens from variables.css (no hardcoded colors/sizes)
js/sections/CompetitiveSection.js exports a class with reveal(), hide(), destroy(), isVisible() methods
index.html contains section#competitive-section positioned after section#why-now-section
The competitive section has exactly 5 advantage blocks: Community Graph, Trust Graph, AI Learning Loop, Creator Ecosystem, Platform Flywheel
Platform Flywheel has an inline SVG with 7 nodes in a cycle, visually distinct from the business section flywheel (uses --color-brand-secondary instead of --color-brand-primary)
Bridge text reads '[Now let us understand the size of the opportunity.]'
All content is placeholder copy (wrapped in brackets)
Reduced motion media query disables all transitions
Responsive: 1 column mobile, 2 columns at 768px, layout adjusts at 1024px
No Canvas, no Three.js used anywhere
No function exceeds 60 lines, no class exceeds 400 lines
HTML uses semantic headings (h2 for section title, h3 for advantage titles)
All [data-reveal] elements have corresponding reveal CSS rules
verification: Run: NODE_OPTIONS='' npx vite build -- confirms no syntax errors in HTML/CSS/JS imports
Verify section order in index.html: why-now-section appears before competitive-section
Verify competitive.css uses only var(--*) tokens and no hardcoded pixel values for colors
Confirm the flywheel SVG in competitive-section uses --color-brand-secondary stroke while business section uses --color-brand-primary
findings: Build verification via vite build was not possible due to INTEGRATIONS_ONLY network mode (npm registry blocked, no node_modules installed). Verified via Node.js syntax checking (--check flag), module import validation, and automated content/structure checks. All acceptance criteria confirmed: 5 advantage blocks present, flywheel SVG uses --color-brand-secondary (distinct from business section --color-brand-primary), bridge text correct, responsive breakpoints and reduced motion included, BEM naming with design tokens only, no hardcoded values.
